obligations.note: The new branch in is_allowed grants any action named 'report:<x>' whenever (role, x) is granted. Actions outside ACTIONS and outside controls/payments/access-policy.json (e.g. 'report:approve_payment' for payments_officer) are now allowed instead of denied, so the effective grants no longer equal the approved policy and default-deny is broken.

Reading GRANTS, the auditor still gets no state-changing base action through the prefix. However, the only exhaustive control-test evidence is a JUnit report that cannot be tied to the head commit (see CHG-4).
it_admin has no approve_payment or release_payment grant, so the prefix should not confer them. The exhaustive control test result relied on is not shown to have run on 88734df (see CHG-4).

rbac.py is in scope, but PRIVILEGED is unchanged and is not prefix-aware, so any 'report:' action would not be treated as privileged. Routes.py is unchanged, and there is no valid CI evidence on the head commit to establish the route table is unaffected.
Ticket CHG-24788 is standard, approved by change manager Grace Kim on 2026-10-23 before review. Its components [payments.access] cover the only touched file, rbac.py.
Mara Costa, a payments change_approver who is not the author Jonah Weiss under any of his addresses, gave a code_review approval.
The code_review and security_review approvals both name head 88734df, the only commit on the change.

run.json claims a run on 88734df by ci-runner-05 starting at the exact commit time. The attached JUnit report is timestamped 2026-10-23T20:50Z, more than a day before the commit, on host dev-laptop-7.local. It is therefore not a CI result for the final commit, and no valid passing suite or control-test run on the final commit exists.
rbac.py (payments.access) is security_sensitive. Kofi Mensah (security_reviewer) gave a security_review approval on the head commit.
No ledger entry covers rbac.py; the entries cover payments.py, audit.py, routes.py and mortgage files. No accepted evidence lapses through this change.

summary: The change adds a 'report:' prefix path to is_allowed. This makes actions that are absent from the approved access policy allowed whenever the base action is granted, which breaks the default-deny, approved-matrix requirement of ACC-1. The CI evidence is also invalid: the JUnit report predates the commit and comes from a developer machine, not the recorded CI run on the head commit, so CHG-4 fails and the other access-related obligations cannot be established. The ticket and the independent code and security approvals are otherwise in order. The change is rejected.
